description:
Stream any VaM camera to OBS as an MJPEG video feed over HTTP. No Spout, no NDI, no native DLLs -- just a URL that any browser or OBS Browser Source can open.

This is a maintained fork of LiveStreamConnectorToOBS by MahiroOyama (CC BY), rebuilt around a raw TcpListener so the stream can reach other devices on the network without elevation or a URL ACL.

What this fork adds over the original:
- Allow Network Access: bind all interfaces instead of loopback only, so a phone, tablet or a second PC can view the stream. The original was localhost-only.
- Access Key: optional shared secret required as ?key=... on every request; unauthorised requests get 403.
- Sync Capture: a toggle that swaps the async GPU readback for an immediate ReadPixels, roughly tripling stream framerate at a cost in game framerate. Measure both and keep the winner.
- Live diagnostics: the Status line reports game fps, stream fps, encode ms, re-render ms and connected client count once a second, so you can see which cost dominates before changing anything.
- Enforced 4-client cap, request timeouts and bounded send buffers, so a slow viewer drops frames instead of stalling the server.

How it works: a small in-VaM HTTP server publishes the chosen camera's render texture as a multipart/x-mixed-replace MJPEG stream. The plugin reads the source camera's existing targetTexture where one is present, so VaM's full render pipeline -- SSSS, hair, clothing, custom passes -- is preserved exactly as already drawn, with no second render. A 256-entry CPU lookup table handles Linear-to-sRGB conversion when the source render texture is in VaM's Linear colour space.

Why not Spout? VaM's DynamicCSharp blocks P/Invoke in user scripts, so a native Spout sender cannot be written as a VaM plugin. MJPEG over HTTP needs no DLLs and no Spout runtime, and works with any OBS install.

Known limitations: the listener is IPv4 only; 'Create New Camera' currently streams black, so pick an existing camera; and dragging the Width, Height or Port controls restarts the server on each frame of the drag, briefly dropping connected clients.
credits:
Original plugin: MahiroOyama (https://hub.virtamate.com/members/mahirooyama.27972/), released as LiveStreamConnectorToOBS under CC BY. This fork keeps the original capture pipeline and camera scanner and rewrites the HTTP server.

Built on VaM's MVRScript (MeshVR) plugin framework.
instructions:
1. Install
   Drop the VAR file into VaM's AddonPackages folder and start VaM.

2. Add the plugin
   Select any atom, open Plugins, Add Plugin, and pick LiveStreamConnectorToOBS.cslist.

3. Pick a source camera
   Open the Source Camera dropdown and choose an existing camera. Cameras that already own a render texture -- a WindowCamera, or a CUA phone screen -- are free to capture, because the plugin just reads what was already drawn. Entries are labelled with their resolution and parent atom. Avoid 'Create New Camera', which currently streams black.

4. Copy the URL
   The OBS URL field always shows the correct URL for the current settings, including host and access key. Default is http://localhost:8088/stream.

5. Wire up OBS
   Add a Browser Source, paste the URL, set its Width and Height to match the plugin's Width and Height, and untick 'Shutdown source when not visible'.

6. Tune it
   Read the Status line for a few seconds before changing anything. If 'render' is above a few ms your source camera has no render texture -- pick a different one. If 'encode' is high, lower Width and Height first, then JPEG Quality. Target FPS is a ceiling, not a guarantee.

7. Stream to another device
   Turn on Allow Network Access to bind all interfaces, set an Access Key, and use the URL shown in the OBS URL field. An inbound firewall rule for the port may be required. Note this publishes a live view of your scene to anything that can route to the host, and the key travels in clear text over plain HTTP.
